page: Google Cloud Platform c3-highmem-192-metal is a bare-metal server instance configured with 192 dedicated virtual CPUs and 1,536 GB of DDR5 memory. The hardware is powered by Intel Xeon 8481C processors running on the x86_64 architecture at 4.0 GHz across 96 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading enabled. The CPU subsystem features 48 KB of L1 data cache per core, 2 MB of L2 cache per core, and a shared 105 MB L3 cache. Instruction set extensions include AVX-512, AMX (Tile and INT8), AES, VAES, and SHA-NI. The instance contains no integrated GPUs and includes no local storage, requiring network-attached storage solutions.

Benchmark results demonstrate exceptional multi-core throughput and memory bandwidth. The instance achieves top-tier results in stress-ng multi-core CPU testing (160,631.15) and PassMark CPU score (125,054.48), backed by extensive extended instructions (191,386.39) and encryption performance (166,616.23). Memory throughput reaches 464.93 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads and 201.86 GB/sec for uncached large-block writes, leading to top-tier Redis SET performance of 181.93 million operations per second and high static web serving throughput of 131.23 GB/sec. Conversely, single-core execution is average in stress-ng (1,987.3) but strong in Geekbench (2,136.0).

Cost efficiency is tied directly to its high-density architecture. With an 8:1 memory-to-core allocation (8.0 GB RAM per vCPU), this bare-metal platform offers high computational and in-memory capacity on dedicated hardware without hypervisor overhead. However, the lack of bundled local NVMe storage and absence of complimentary public IPv4 addresses introduce additional infrastructure considerations.

This server type is suited for large-scale in-memory databases, high-throughput database operations, large memory-bound caching layers, extensive software compilation, and parallel enterprise workloads that benefit from direct hardware access and AMX/AVX-512 instruction extensions.
description: Google Cloud Platform c3-highmem-192-metal is a bare-metal server offering 192 dedicated vCPUs (96 physical cores) powered by Intel Xeon 8481C processors running at 4.0 GHz on the x86_64 architecture, paired with 1,536 GB of DDR5 RAM. Operating without a virtualization hypervisor, it includes AMX and AVX-512 vector support, but contains no local storage and zero GPUs. Benchmark evaluations show top-tier results in multi-core compute metrics, such as a PassMark CPU score of 125,054.48, and exceptional memory performance yielding 464.93 GB/sec uncached reads and 181.93 million Redis SET operations per second. Its massive 8 GB per vCPU memory density provides substantial qualitative value for memory-heavy parallel systems, though external storage must be provisioned separately. It is engineered primarily for in-memory databases, large-scale Redis deployments, enterprise analytics, and compute-intensive compilation pipelines.
